reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the webinar promotes paid OneCoin packages, including a EUR 1,000 purchase for tokens, and links participation to required purchases, package-sale qualifications, and recruitment-linked bonuses. It also presents optimistic future-value projections and unusually large, time-bound earnings claims, while the described tokens, splits, earnings, and rewards are not established as delivered or independently verified.

citations.quote: a token is a right to extract a coin in Onecoin
you buy a package for 1000 euros
to become the crowned diamond you need to have 6 black diamonds in the frontline
those people who really build a network actively enough will get the biggest rewards here from the investment

opening.argument: The presentation does not present every outcome as certain. Its growth chart explicitly distinguishes an “Optimistic Scenario” from a “Base Scenario” and includes a disclaimer that the result depends on loyalty and continued user-base growth. The speaker also qualifies his blockchain discussion, saying he is not a banker and has read only a few articles. Those qualifications frame the material as conditional commentary and a forecast, not a guaranteed return or certification that every projection will occur.

citations.quote: I'm not a banker myself and, even, and don't take it very literally. I've read a few articles on blockchain

rebuttal.rebuttal: The package table shows prices and token allocations, but that alone does not establish deception or a guaranteed return. The cited leadership language describes rewards for activity, while the chart visibly labels its figures as scenarios and includes a growth disclaimer. The material therefore can be read as conditional promotion and financial commentary whose results depend on future adoption, rather than as a promise that purchasers will certainly profit.

citations.quote: those people who really build a network actively enough will get the biggest rewards here from the investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not neutralize the underlying solicitation. The presentation still says a token is a right to extract a coin, gives a EUR 1,000 package example, and describes doubling through splits. A forecast disclaimer may qualify future value, but it does not change that viewers are asked to pay for access to purported mining-related benefits.

you buy a package for 1000 euros
this is essentially doubling money

opening.argument: The video can reasonably be understood as an educational webinar explaining cryptocurrency concepts and the proposed operation of a platform. It describes recorded Academy modules covering cryptocurrency, finances, risks, and gold investment, while the slides present explanations of mining, tokens, and an exchange interface. The speaker also says questions are to be held until the end, which is consistent with a structured presentation and demonstration. Its central observable activity is explaining how the proposed system works, not documenting a completed result.

citations.quote: through this Academy, using special video modules, using PDF files
in the Academy you can learn about risks, what finances are, what cryptocurrency iso currency is, what the investment in gold is
For those who don't know what Mining is, I'll have another part on this topic

rebuttal.rebuttal: The webinar's instructional format does not by itself make it ordinary education. It presents paid packages, token allocations, and a route from tokens to coins. It also describes concrete commissions and package-based qualifications. Those are not merely technical demonstrations; they are presented as reasons to participate in the business.

citations.quote: Those tokens are the path to the coin mining.
to become the crowned diamond you need to have 6 black diamonds in the frontline

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the material educational does not remove its commercial purpose. The Academy slide specifically teaches viewers how to obtain profit by trading tokens and cryptocurrency, and the speaker connects education to tokens that permit mining. The presentation therefore uses instruction to promote a paid financial opportunity, rather than offering neutral technical education.

citations.quote: OneCoin Academy is what we get as a product, plus we get tokens.
Those tokens are the path to the coin mining.

opening.argument: The offer is also consistent with ordinary commerce: a purchaser receives an Academy package and associated digital items, while registration itself is described as free for people who want to study and ask questions. The presentation identifies a product, package levels, prices, and an exchange where tokens can be bought or sold. The supplied material does not establish that every purchaser is guaranteed a return, that a credential or personal information must be surrendered, or that a completed payout is required to obtain the educational product. Those gaps matter before classifying the offer as inherently fraudulent.

citations.quote: You can register for free to get acquainted, study, and ask questions.
OneCoin Academy is what we get as a product, plus we get tokens.
a token is a financial product, which you can buy on the OneExchange exchange

rebuttal.rebuttal: The free registration option does not answer what paying customers are being sold. The package table shows that higher-priced packages supply tokens, and the presentation expressly links those tokens to extracting coins. It also conditions promotions on selling packages and reaching business volume. Those features go beyond an ordinary standalone course or retail service.

citations.quote: Those tokens are the path to the coin mining.
sell 2 packages of Tycoon or 10 packages of Protrader for 1000 $EUR.
then you and the hotel will be paid.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged product cannot be separated from the financial inducement. The presentation says tokens grant the right to extract OneCoin, gives a EUR 1,000 purchase example, and requires token purchases from part of commission payments. A free introductory registration does not make the paid mining-related package ordinary commerce or show that the promised digital benefits were delivered.
